parts.text: A box contains 5 red counters and 3 blue counters. One counter is removed at random and not replaced. A green counter is then added to the box. A second counter is then removed at random. Given that the second counter is blue, find the probability that the first counter removed was red.

Box A contains 4 white discs and 2 black discs. Box B contains 3 white discs and 5 black discs. One disc is selected at random from Box A and transferred to Box B. A disc is then selected at random from Box B. Given that the disc selected from Box B is black, find the probability that a black disc was transferred from Box A.

A commuter records whether their morning train is on time over three consecutive days: Day 1, Day 2, and Day 3. On Day 1, the probability that the train is on time is $\frac{4}{5}$. If the train is on time on any day, the probability that it is on time on the following day is $\frac{3}{4}$. If the train is late on any day, the probability that it is on time on the following day is $\frac{1}{2}$. Find the probability that the train is on time on Day 3.

An archer takes three shots at a target. On the first shot, the probability of hitting the bullseye is $0.4$. If she hits the bullseye on any shot, the probability of hitting the bullseye on the next shot is $0.6$. If she misses on any shot, the probability of hitting the bullseye on the next shot is $0.3$. Given that she hits the bullseye on the first shot, find the probability that she hits the bullseye on exactly two of the three shots.

Bag 1 contains 3 red marbles and 2 blue marbles. Bag 2 contains 2 red marbles and 4 blue marbles. A bag is chosen at random with equal probability. One marble is drawn at random from the chosen bag and not replaced. One yellow marble is then placed into the chosen bag. Finally, a second marble is drawn from the chosen bag. Find the probability that the second marble drawn is yellow.

questions.topic: Alternating game without replacement with stopping rule

parts.text: A bag contains 3 red counters and 3 blue counters. Amy and Ben take turns removing one counter at random without replacement, with Amy drawing first. The game ends immediately when a player removes a red counter, and that player wins. Find the probability that Amy wins on her second turn.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A box initially contains 4 red balls and 2 green balls. A ball is chosen at random and removed from the box. Two yellow balls are then placed into the box. A second ball is then chosen at random from the box. Find the probability that the second ball chosen is yellow.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that the second ball chosen is yellow, find the probability that the first ball chosen was red.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Urn X contains 5 red discs and 3 blue discs. Urn Y contains 2 red discs and 4 blue discs. One disc is selected at random from Urn X and transferred into Urn Y. A disc is then selected at random from Urn Y. Find the probability that the disc selected from Urn Y is red.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that the disc selected from Urn Y is red, find the probability that the disc transferred from Urn X was blue.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a certain town, each day is either Sunny ($S$) or Rainy ($R$). On Monday, the probability that it is Sunny is $0.7$. If it is Sunny on any day, the probability that the next day is Sunny is $0.8$. If it is Rainy on any day, the probability that the next day is Sunny is $0.3$. Find the probability that it is Sunny on Wednesday.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that it is Rainy on Wednesday, find the probability that it was Sunny on Monday.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A basketball player takes three consecutive free throws. The probability that he scores on the first throw is $0.6$. If he scores on any throw, the probability that he scores on the next throw is $0.7$. If he misses on any throw, the probability that he scores on the next throw is $0.4$. Find the probability that he scores on at least two of the three throws.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that he scores on at least two of the three throws, find the probability that he scored on his first throw.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A fair six-sided die is rolled. If a 1 or 2 is rolled, Bag A is selected; otherwise, Bag B is selected. Bag A contains 4 red counters and 2 white counters. Bag B contains 3 red counters and 5 white counters. A counter is removed at random from the selected bag and not replaced. One black counter is then placed into that bag. Finally, a second counter is removed at random from the same bag. Find the probability that both counters removed are red.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that both counters removed are red, find the probability that Bag A was selected.

questions.topic: Alternating two-player game with target win condition

parts.label: a
parts.text: A pouch contains 4 gold coins and 4 silver coins. Leo and Mia take turns drawing one coin at random without replacement, with Leo drawing first. The game ends as soon as one player accumulates a total of two gold coins, and that player wins. Find the probability that Leo wins on his second turn (Draw 3).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the probability that Mia wins on her second turn (Draw 4).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Given that the game ends on or before Draw 4, find the probability that Leo was the winner.

questions.topic: Two-way urn transfer cascade and Bayesian inversion

parts.label: a
parts.text: Box 1 initially contains 3 red counters and 3 green counters. Box 2 initially contains 4 red counters and 2 green counters. In Step 1, one counter is chosen at random from Box 1 and transferred to Box 2. In Step 2, one counter is chosen at random from Box 2 and transferred back into Box 1. Find the probability that the counter transferred in Step 2 was red.

parts.label: b
parts.text: In Step 3, a final counter is chosen at random from Box 1. Find the probability that this final counter is red.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Given that the final counter chosen from Box 1 in Step 3 is red, find the probability that the counter transferred in Step 1 was red.
